newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's top court definitively sentences Craxi.
newsitem.headline: Italy's top court definitively sentences Craxi.

text.p: Italy's highest court on Tuesday upheld prison sentences against former prime minister Bettino Craxi and nine others in the country's first definitive ruling in more than three years of graft scandals.
The Cassation Court confirmed the conviction of Craxi and nine others on corruption charges relating to bribes paid by insurance company SAI to win an insurance contract from state energy group ENI.

The conviction, which sentences Craxi to five and a half years in prison for illegal party financing, was upheld on appeal last May but is only now definite. The Cassation Court is the final stage of appeal in Italian law.

The court also confirmed sentences against financier Sergio Cusani, former SAI president Salvatore Ligresti and managing director Fausto Rapisardo, former Christian Democrat party treasurer Severino Citaristi and two former ENI executives.
Citaristi, like Craxi, faced five and a half years in jail while Cusani's sentence was for four years. The others had jail terms of less than three years.
The court said it had reversed previous convictions of Rinaldo Petrignani, a former Rome ambassador to Washington, and lawyer Giuseppe Sbisa because "the crimes attributed to them do not exist".
Former Socialist Craxi, 64, lives in self-imposed exile in the Tunisian resort of Hammamet, saying he is too ill with diabetes to return home.
He has appeals pending against three other court convictions, for which he has been sentenced to prison terms totalling an additional 20 years and three months.
Prime minister from 1983 to 1987, Craxi became one of Italy's most reviled public figures when the old political guard was brought down in a series of corruption probes. He has denied any wrongdoing.

Last April, after being sentenced to eight years and three months in jail and fined $23 million in a graft scandal over the building of Milan's underground railway, Craxi said there was "an organised political persecution" against him.
